Trail River is separately labelled at the joining vicinity, and the selected lower course continues north to the Babbage delta.
The observed terminal enters southern Phillips Bay; Babbage Bight is a separately labelled coastal water area to the east.

sources.title: Plan de Manejo del Área Natural Protegida Meseta de Somuncurá, Provincia de Río Negro; Decreto 465/2008, Boletín Oficial de Río Negro 4634, suplemento, 3 de julio de 2008
sources.publisher: Gobierno de Río Negro; Consejo de Ecología y Medio Ambiente
sources.publication_identity_basis: An independently commissioned protected-area management project approved by Decreto465/2008. The original describes its own thematic GIS, Landsat interpretation and FUNDAL GPS fieldwork. A surviving normally acquired original was read locally; no new request or stopped geological-sheet original was used.
sources.actual_material_read: Original front matter/decree and title; hydrological text on printed pages35–36; GIS methodology on printed77; Map1 on printed36; original full-page and northeastern views of Caminos, ferrocarril y poblaciones en el ANP on120 and Espejos y Cursos de aguas sobre curvas de nivel on124, including the map axes and northern extent. Relevant bibliography was inspected as bibliography only.
observations: The plan describes temporarily occupied closed depressions and linear arroyo/cañadón drainage in the Somuncurá region.

Its basin account separately associates Yaminué, Treneta and Comicó with Indio Muerto, and Chasicó, Paja Alta and Valcheta with Curicó. These are adjacent regional relationships, not selected-route names.

The GIS methodology expressly specifies UTM Zone19 South. The displayed northern map frame lies south of the supplied selection, so the annex cannot establish the selected opening, course or endpoint.
sources.limits: This is a successfully read adjacent-region source with a geographic coverage mismatch for the present target. It supplies no affirmative selected-channel correspondence. Its regional drainage names are not whole-feature identity evidence.

correspondence.component_scope: Chosen northern opening and early southward Canadian traverse
correspondence.finding: The federal reference view is largely blank over this Canadian selection. Read regional prose establishes a mountain-and-icefield setting, but it does not locate the chosen opening or distinguish its sequence of ice corridors. No original Canadian map pixels were successfully read.

correspondence.component_scope: Remaining Canadian southward and eastward traverse to the Alaska border
correspondence.finding: The selected Canadian bends and their complete connection to the mapped U.S. Hubbard corridor remain without readable cartographic correspondence. Blank map coverage is a material-content limitation, not an access failure. Glacier proximity or the modeled connection is not substituted for the missing source coverage.

correspondence.component_scope: U.S. portion of the first mainstem fragment and its join to the second
correspondence.finding: The original depicts the southeastern border entry and adjoining mountain-bounded ice corridor continuously into the labelled Hubbard Glacier. This establishes the selected U.S. terrain passage at ordinary corridor scale, without asserting a natural river channel or exact ice-flow line.

correspondence.component_scope: Second mainstem fragment through the Hubbard Glacier corridor
correspondence.finding: The full selected north–south passage lies within the mapped Hubbard ice corridor, alongside mountain projections, and reaches the eastern ice-margin join. The neighbouring Valerie, Miller and Turner glaciers are separately mapped and are not substituted for this selection.

correspondence.component_scope: Entire eastern tributary fragment and common ice-margin join
correspondence.finding: The tributary selection starts on mapped ice east of the main selected route, follows the eastern mountain margin and meets the main selection at the southern ice edge. All of its parts have readable terrain coverage. No distinct river or tributary-glacier name is established for this line.

correspondence.component_scope: Final mainstem fragment through the ice-margin and coastal setting to its actual terminal
correspondence.finding: The final selection follows the eastern ice margin, crosses a mapped lowland and wetland/outwash setting near the Variegated Glacier drainage, then ends within water labelled Russell Fiord. Disenchantment Bay is the separate western waterbody beyond the Gilbert Point peninsula. This terrain correspondence does not demonstrate one continuous named river or a present ice-front position.

correspondence.component_scope: Chosen headward opening and southeast-oriented inland feeder
correspondence.finding: The municipal original depicts the headwater drainage network and the southeast-oriented feeder corridor into the eastward inland watercourse. The selected opening was considered in the original-map enlargement. No hydronym is established for this initial feeder; the nearby municipal-boundary river is not substituted for it.

correspondence.component_scope: Inland eastward course toward the settled Pracuúba lowland
correspondence.finding: The original municipal map shows the eastward drainage corridor through Floresta Estadual do Amapá and toward the Pernambuco/Flexal locality setting. The locality labels Flexal and Flechal do not themselves name every selected river reach.

correspondence.component_scope: Southward turn and approach to the western lake arms near Ponta Baixa
correspondence.finding: The municipal original depicts the drainage and lake-arm setting west and southwest of Pracuúba, including Ponta Baixa. The selected broad approach is recognizable, but its complete connection into and through the lake complex is not established by that regional depiction alone.

correspondence.component_scope: Lake passage and northbound exit past the Pracuúba settlement setting
correspondence.finding: The municipal map exposes multiple connected lake arms around Pracuúba and Ponta Baixa. It does not establish the full selected through-passage and its direct northern continuation toward the São Miguel do Flexal wetland corridor. A label for the entire selected lake complex is not assigned.

correspondence.component_scope: Long northbound lowland/wetland connector
correspondence.finding: Rio Flechal is directly labelled in municipal cartography, and the sanitation study distinguishes it from Rio Amapá Pequeno and describes their junction. However, the selected northbound connector is not continuously matched to the depicted Flechal course. The mere presence of the named river nearby is insufficient to complete this component.

correspondence.component_scope: Eastward wetland/lake crossing before the fragment join
correspondence.finding: The selected route turns east through the coastal lake/wetland setting. The municipal map depicts lakes and separate small drainage branches there, while the sanitation figures show the Flechal continuing farther north past the Amapá Pequeno junction. Neither original establishes the complete selected eastward through-link. The study's Lago Bom Nome reference is regional context only, not proof that every selected lake segment belongs to that lake.

correspondence.component_scope: Final northeast reach, inter-fragment continuation and explicit selected sea endpoint
correspondence.finding: The second fragment and its actual sea endpoint were considered separately from the longer inland fragment. Its coastal ending lies south of the independently depicted Igarapé do Garrote outlet and east of the Flechal corridor. The originals do not show a continuous selected channel from the eastern lake/wetland crossing to this coast point. No alternate mapped river mouth was substituted for the selected terminal.

correspondence.component_scope: Chosen western opening, initial southeastern descent and eastward bend
correspondence.finding: The selected opening and initial southern/eastward course are outside the acquired Herschel Island map. No independent original cartography was inspected for these parts or their intervening joins. Their connection to the named downstream river is not established by this pass.

correspondence.component_scope: Upper and middle northeastern course and successive joins
correspondence.finding: This long selected valley interval is south of the inspected map. The downstream Babbage label does not establish the chosen headward branch or these through-links.

correspondence.component_scope: Eastern approach and transition into the northern map
correspondence.finding: Most of this eastern approach is outside the acquired map. The final part crosses its southern edge into the visible Babbage corridor, but the southern approach and whole cross-edge join were not compared with an adjoining original.

correspondence.component_scope: Northern turn, westward reach and Trail River joining vicinity
correspondence.finding: The original shows the selected turn from the southern edge into a northwestward and then westward reach of Babbage River. The joining vicinity of the separately labelled Trail River and the subsequent northward continuation agree at ordinary corridor scale.

correspondence.component_scope: Lower northward Babbage River and coastal-plain joins
correspondence.finding: The labelled Babbage course continues north across the coastal plain. Its northward bends and adjacent Deep Creek network correspond to the selected lower corridor; the neighboring rivers and ponds are distinguishable from this course.

correspondence.component_scope: Northwestern delta course and actual coastal ending
correspondence.finding: The selected final westward and northwestern course corresponds to the mapped Babbage delta entering the southern side of Phillips Bay, west of the Babbage Bight coast. The river-to-bay continuation is visible at ordinary regional scale; individual modern distributary banks and exact shoreline positions are not assigned.

correspondence.component_scope: Northwestern chosen opening and first southeast approach
correspondence.finding: The pinned opening and first four parts form the northwestern approach. They lie north of the inspected Somuncurá map coverage. The source supplies no channel, headwater identity or initial drainage connection for this selection.

correspondence.component_scope: Long upper eastward reach and southeast turn
correspondence.finding: The selection continues through a substantial easterly interval and then turns southeast. No inspected independent cartography establishes the selected through-course, its contributing channels or the connection across this upper interval. Adjacent regional basin names are not substituted for those links.

correspondence.component_scope: Southward bend and middle southeast corridor
correspondence.finding: The selected line makes a short southerly bend and then runs southeast through ten stored parts. The readable management-plan maps end to the south and cannot identify this corridor or demonstrate the intervening joins. Discovery of a possible local name was not promoted to evidence.

correspondence.component_scope: Northeast reversal and subsequent eastward middle reach
correspondence.finding: The selection reverses toward the northeast, turns east, and resumes a southeast trend. Neither the selected reversal nor the through-link across the intervening lowland is established by an inspected source. No lake, wetland, saline-flat or dry-channel passage is inferred from the modeled line alone.

correspondence.component_scope: Lower southeast approach
correspondence.finding: The selected lower line trends southeast through a sequence of short parts. Its ordinary channel identity, tributary joins and any depression or saline-flat passage are unresolved. The stopped article supplied no readable source body or map, and its discovery excerpts do not establish this lower course.

correspondence.component_scope: Final southern bend, eastward leg and actual internal endpoint
correspondence.finding: The preserved selection bends south and then east/northeast before terminating internally. No inspected source identifies the actual selected terminal or establishes its entry into a named receiving waterbody or salt flat. The endpoint is not reassigned to the nearest discovered regional feature.
